title: Homeostasis and Hormones
seo_title: Year 11 Science: Homeostasis and Hormones Worksheets (GCSE Combined Science)
standard_text: Homeostasis and control systems; the structure and function of the nervous system and reflex arcs; reaction time; the endocrine system; control of blood glucose concentration and diabetes; hormones in human reproduction and contraception; (higher tier) adrenaline, thyroxine and negative feedback.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE Combined Science worksheets on homeostasis: reflex arcs, reaction time, hormones, blood glucose, diabetes, the menstrual cycle and contraception. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Homeostasis keeps the body's conditions constant.
key_sub: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Nerves are fast; hormones are slower and last longer.

  • Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neurone → relay neurone → motor neurone → effector.
  • Blood glucose too high → insulin (glucose stored as glycogen). Too low → glucagon (glycogen → glucose).
  • FSH matures an egg, LH causes ovulation, oestrogen and progesterone build and keep the uterus lining.
Example

Blood glucose 11 mmol/L. Hormone?

Above 4–7

Too high

Answer: insulin

Example

Reaction times 0.24, 0.26, 0.28 s. Mean?

0.78 ÷ 3

Answer: 0.26 s

Common mistakes

  • Thinking glucagon lowers blood glucose.
  • Thinking hormones travel along nerves.
  • Thinking the sensory neurone carries impulses to the muscle.

faq.q: What happens in a reflex arc?
faq.a: A receptor detects a stimulus, a sensory neurone carries the impulse to the spinal cord, a relay neurone passes it on, and a motor neurone carries it to an effector.
The pancreas releases insulin when glucose is high and glucagon when it is low. Both act on the liver.

faq.q: What is the difference between type 1 and type 2 diabetes?
faq.a: In type 1 the pancreas makes too little insulin. In type 2 the body cells stop responding to insulin.

items.q: Platelets calling more platelets to a cut until it clots is an example of which kind of feedback?

items.e: Negative feedback keeps conditions stable.

items.e: The chemical triggers an impulse in the next neurone.
